items.title: Deja vu here as nearly this exact info was ‘reported’ a year ago. more likely to be true this time, but manufacturing at scale is the easy part for Tesla. What matters is whether the optimus humanoid hardware platform can deliver the performance and KPIs to justify deployment at any scale. Curious what Tesla intends to do with 5,000 bots, as it would take up to 15,000 human operators to put them into 24/7 training. Cautiously optimistic, but keeping the thesis tethered to observable reality.
items.content:
Deja vu here as nearly this exact info was ‘reported’ a year ago. more likely to be true this time, but manufacturing at scale is the easy part for Tesla. What matters is whether the optimus humanoid hardware platform can deliver the performance and KPIs to justify deployment at any scale.

Curious what Tesla intends to do with 5,000 bots, as it would take up to 15,000 human operators to put them into 24/7 training.

Cautiously optimistic, but keeping the thesis tethered to observable reality.Ming (@tslaming)GOOD NEWS 🤖 According to supply-chain vendors and today’s report by Jiemian News, Tesla has issued an initial batch order for roughly 5,000 Optimus robots 🔥

Following earlier pilot runs of just a few hundred units, this marks the program's first production order in the thousands. The new order establishes a firm baseline delivery target of around 15,000 units this year. 

More importantly, it signals a critical pivot: the supply chain is moving past merely proving the robot can be built and into the phase of testing real volume manufacturing.

The immediate hurdle is a crucial round of domestic supplier audits scheduled for September—Tesla's standard gateway for bumping vendors from provisional status to certified mass-production partners.

That timing fits right into Tesla’s procurement guidance, which calls for suppliers to hit a run rate of 1,000 units per week in September, ramping up to between 2,000 and 2,500 weekly by year-end.

While Tesla has a track record of sliding timelines, this milestone carries different weight. With purchase orders officially cut, audits on the calendar, and suppliers actively stocking inventory, the program is shifting from executive talk to real execution on the factory floor.—  https://x.com/tslaming/status/2096977354044432895 
— Chris Camillo (@ChrisCamillo) Sep 7, 2026

items.title: Been getting the same pushback on my $TSLA cybercab take for yrs: “you just don’t get it.” Meanwhile, the opportunity cost of parking capital in $TSLA during this period of stratospheric returns across AI winners would have been catastrophic. If robotaxi starts showing signs of being 5x bigger than I’m modeling, or when optimus materializes, I’ll happily lean into the trade late. Until then, I’m continue to allocate capital where I have better visibility into what I can actually observe vs. speculative scenarios that are years out. no hate to the tesla fanboys. your win if it happens won’t be my loss
